items.title: Your brain on AI
items.excerpt: MIT Technology Review pulls together what cognitive research now says about offloading thinking to chatbots: the measurable effects on memory, attention and the feeling of understanding. It is the clearest current read on what daily AI use does to human cognition.

items.title: AI boosts sensitivity to double-Higgs signatures occurring about once per trillion collisions
items.excerpt: A University of Michigan-led team used a graph neural network to lift sensitivity to rare double-Higgs events at the LHC by about 65% over previous analyses. It is a concrete case of deep learning changing what a physics experiment can actually see.

items.title: Machine learning method uncovers hidden patterns in DNA methylation
items.excerpt: metilene3 finds differentially methylated DNA regions without needing samples pre-labelled healthy or diseased. It reconstructed immune-cell developmental pathways, separated tumour subgroups and traced pancreatic cancer progression.

items.title: Chatbots are making our writing more similar but losing the identity and personality behind it
items.excerpt: When LLMs rewrite text they cut variation in writing complexity by 21-50% while keeping meaning intact. Models reading the rewritten passages became six percentage points worse at inferring the author's personal traits - a warning for language-based psychological assessment.

items.title: DigBat: An AI-ready digital platform for solid-state battery research
items.excerpt: Tohoku University's DigBat merges 3,816 experimental solid-state electrolytes (27,645 conductivity entries) with 852 computational materials into a single machine-learning-ready database. It is the data layer autonomous materials labs have been missing.

items.title: Who does AI consider an expert? New benchmark shows bias across 22 LLMs
items.excerpt: A Complexity Science Hub benchmark tested 22 large language models on who they name as an expert. The models did not merely mirror existing inequality - they amplified it, under-representing women and scholars from under-represented backgrounds.

items.title: Fruit fly-inspired algorithm classifies odors from only a few samples
items.excerpt: OIST's Spi-Fly borrows the fruit fly's olfactory circuit to classify smells from very few training samples. The result is a low-power, few-shot route to machine olfaction that does not need a huge labelled dataset.

items.title: FDA digital health leader promises generative AI regulatory guidance is coming
items.excerpt: FDA's digital health lead says formal guidance on generative AI in medical products is being drafted. It signals the shift from case-by-case clearance to a written rulebook for LLMs in clinical settings.

items.title: AI is good at catching drug theft at hospitals, but only when humans do their part
items.excerpt: Hospital drug-diversion detection models flag theft well in principle, but performance collapses when the human review loop is thin. A useful field study of where AI accuracy stops and organisational process starts.

items.title: A New Framework for How the Brain Compresses Our Noisy World
items.excerpt: A new theory of predictive categorization describes how brains throw away most sensory detail and keep only what predicts the future. The framing maps directly onto how representation learning in neural networks is understood.

items.title: Paving the way for greener ammonia production
items.excerpt: MIT researchers combined density functional theory with machine learning to screen transition-metal nitride alloys for electrochemical ammonia synthesis. The computational screen replaces trial-and-error catalyst search for one of chemistry's largest carbon footprints.

items.title: An AI tool for prioritizing candidate biomarkers from wearable sensor data
items.excerpt: Google Research describes a system that sifts continuous wearable sensor streams to rank which signals are worth testing as real biomarkers. It is hypothesis generation applied to health data that is otherwise too large to inspect.

items.title: From Models to Agents: The Next Phase of AI Adoption in Molecular Discovery
items.excerpt: GEN maps the move in drug discovery from static predictive models to agentic systems that plan and run their own molecular design loops. Includes the concrete agent interfaces vendors are now shipping for protein binder design.

items.title: Protecting Scientific Intent in AI-Enabled Labs by Not Letting AI Set the Mission
items.excerpt: An argument about where autonomy should stop in self-driving labs: automate execution, keep the research question human. A practical governance frame for anyone standing up an autonomous experimentation stack.

items.title: CodonMamba: a foundation model for programmable mRNA coding sequence design
items.excerpt: A state-space foundation model trained to design mRNA coding sequences, aiming at programmable control of expression rather than one-off codon optimization. Preprint from the generative-biology wave now hitting mRNA therapeutics.

items.title: ASAREE: An Analytical Sandbox for Agentic AI Research, Engineering, and Experimentation
items.excerpt: ASAREE proposes a sandbox for running and evaluating agentic AI systems that do their own research, engineering and experimentation. It is infrastructure for testing 'AI co-scientist' claims instead of taking them on trust.

items.title: The physics of novel computation: beyond bits and chips to spikes and spins
items.excerpt: A survey of the physical substrates being proposed to run AI beyond CMOS - spiking neuromorphic devices, spintronics, photonics. Useful context for why model efficiency is becoming a materials-physics problem.

items.title: No quantum advantage (yet) in the world of tensor networks
items.excerpt: Classical tensor-network methods keep matching quantum processors on the tasks meant to demonstrate advantage. A sober checkpoint for anyone tracking quantum machine learning claims.

items.title: How generative AI is reshaping creativity, and what it means for artists
items.excerpt: Scientific American looks at what research on originality says about generative tools - whether models widen the space of ideas or pull output toward the mean. Directly relevant to how creative work gets evaluated.

items.title: Scientists Look to the Brain to Improve Quantum Sensors
items.excerpt: Researchers are borrowing neural coding strategies to squeeze more precision out of quantum sensors. A neuromorphic idea crossing into quantum metrology.

items.title: Why is AI going on a hacking spree?
items.excerpt: Live Science examines the reported surge of AI agents autonomously finding and exploiting vulnerabilities, and what capability actually changed. Relevant to anyone deploying agentic systems with tool access.

items.title: Astro-Hunters: Machine Learning for Exoplanet Transit Detection in TESS Photometry
items.excerpt: Exoplanet hunting is now a data-analysis problem: TESS returns far more light curves than humans can inspect. This work trains classifiers to surface transit candidates automatically from that flood of photometry.

items.title: Radio Galaxies detection and characterization using deep learning techniques
items.excerpt: Next-generation radio telescopes will produce data volumes that defeat traditional statistical pipelines. The paper applies deep learning to detect and characterize radio galaxies at survey scale.

items.title: Interpretable statistical feature engineering for early disruption prediction in tokamaks
items.excerpt: Machine-learning disruption predictors for fusion plasmas usually trade accuracy for opacity. This work builds interpretable statistical features so operators can see why a disruption alarm fired in time to act.
